kept.title: Arbitrary File Write via Zip Slip
kept.description: The extraction logic in src/unpack.ts and src/write-entry.ts fails to effectively sanitize paths containing symbolic links or '../' sequences when `preservePaths` is true, leading to potential path traversal (Zip Slip).
steps_to_exploit: Craft a malicious tar archive containing a file with a path like '../../../../etc/passwd'.
Set the `preservePaths` option to true via the API.
The `Unpack` process will write files outside the intended destination directory.
kept.impact: Attackers can overwrite critical system files, potentially gaining remote code execution or privilege escalation.

kept.title: Use of Deprecated/Thread-Unsafe process.umask()
kept.description: src/process-umask.ts exports a function that calls the deprecated and thread-unsafe `process.umask()`. This creates a global state race condition in multi-threaded or asynchronous environments.
steps_to_exploit: Multiple concurrent extraction operations use `chmod` option.
Each process concurrently modifies the process-wide umask.
The race condition results in incorrect permissions for extracted files.
kept.impact: Security misconfiguration of file permissions, making sensitive files world-readable or writable.

kept.title: Insecure Default File Permissions
kept.description: The `modeFix` function applies a fallback mode of `0o666` which, when combined with `umask`, may result in overly permissive files if not strictly controlled.
steps_to_exploit: Archive is created with default `modeFix` settings.
Files are extracted on a system with a loose or non-standard `umask`.
Files are created with insecure permissions (e.g., group-writable).
kept.impact: Unauthorized modification or unauthorized access to extracted data by other users on the host system.

kept.title: Memory Exhaustion via Large Meta Entries
kept.description: The parser uses a `maxMetaEntrySize` limit but allows up to 1MB. While configurable, the internal string concatenation `this[META] += c` in `parse.ts` can lead to rapid memory pressure if multiple large entries are processed.
steps_to_exploit: Submit a large number of entries with large PAX headers.
The parser stores these in memory via string concatenation.
The process triggers an OOM kill due to memory exhaustion.
kept.impact: Denial of Service (DoS) of the extraction or listing process.

kept.title: Insecure Handling of Symbolic Links During Extraction
kept.description: Although the code attempts to check for symlinks, the `ENSURE_NO_SYMLINK` implementation in `unpack.ts` can be bypassed due to potential TOCTOU (Time-of-Check to Time-of-Use) vulnerabilities during recursive directory creation.
steps_to_exploit: Prepare an archive with a directory entry that is actually a symlink.
The extraction process checks the path, and finds it is a safe directory.
The symlink is created or replaced by an attacker between the check and the final extraction step.
kept.impact: Path traversal or directory clobbering outside the destination folder.

kept.title: Potential Integer Overflow in Large Number Parsing
kept.description: The parsing of base256 encoded numbers in `large-numbers.ts` uses `Math.pow` and standard number multiplication, which might lose precision for very large values before reaching the SafeInteger limit.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a tarball with an entry header containing a massive size field.
The parser processes the value, potentially leading to incorrect file offsets or size calculations.
The logic fails to detect overflow correctly in certain edge cases.
kept.impact: Data corruption or incorrect file extraction offsets, potentially leading to security bypasses.

kept.title: Improper Input Validation for Command Arguments
kept.description: The `makeCommand` wrapper in `make-command.ts` attempts to dynamically determine if arguments are options or file lists by checking `Array.isArray`. This can be manipulated if an attacker can control input structure.
steps_to_exploit: Invoke `tar` methods with user-controlled input as the first argument.
Inject an array where options are expected.
The parser switches context, potentially executing operations with unexpected default configuration.
kept.impact: Unexpected behavior, bypass of configuration settings (like `cwd` or `strict` mode).

kept.title: Insecure Symlink Creation in Unpack
kept.description: The `Unpack` class in `unpack.ts` creates symlinks using `fs.symlink`. It doesn't strictly validate the target path against the extraction root, trusting the `linkpath` provided in the tarball metadata.
steps_to_exploit: Create a tarball where a file entry is a symlink to '/etc/passwd'.
Execute `tar.extract` on the archive.
The system creates a symbolic link pointing to a system file.
kept.impact: Information disclosure or integrity compromise if the symlink is later followed by system services.

kept.title: Cache Poisoning via NormalizeUnicode
kept.description: The `normalizeUnicode` cache in `src/normalize-unicode.ts` is a simple global LRU-like set. It does not consider the source context, leading to potential path normalization collisions.
steps_to_exploit: Use conflicting Unicode characters that normalize to the same sequence.
Force a collision in the cache.
One path's normalization metadata is reused for a different path, confusing the filesystem logic.
kept.impact: File system entry confusion during extraction, potentially leading to overwriting incorrect files.

kept.title: Information Leak through Error Messages
kept.description: The `CwdError` and `SymlinkError` objects include raw file paths and system state information which are emitted in error events.
steps_to_exploit: Trigger an extraction failure (e.g., non-existent directory).
Listen for error events.
Receive detailed paths and system metadata in the error objects.
kept.impact: Exposure of server-side directory structures to the client/user, facilitating reconnaissance.

kept.title: Unsafe Use of Buffer.allocUnsafe
kept.description: Using `Buffer.allocUnsafe` in various parts of the library (e.g., `list.ts`) potentially exposes uninitialized memory if the subsequent read is partial.
steps_to_exploit: Read a file where the read call returns fewer bytes than requested.
The uninitialized part of the buffer is retained.
The parser or subsequent consumer processes the sensitive data (if any was in memory).
kept.impact: Potential information leakage of previously allocated memory contents.

kept.title: Symlink Attack through Hardlinks
kept.description: The logic in `WriteEntry` and `Unpack` regarding hardlinks can be manipulated to link to files that were intended to be restricted.
steps_to_exploit: Include both a file and a hardlink in a tarball.
The parser processes them, creating links on the target filesystem.
The hardlink mechanism might create links to unauthorized system files if the path sanitization is bypassed.
kept.impact: Integrity compromise; unintended files made accessible/writable via hardlinks.

kept.title: Missing Error Handling in Synchronous Close
kept.description: Several `finally` blocks swallow errors during file descriptor closure (e.g., `list.ts`).
steps_to_exploit: Trigger an extraction that exhausts system file descriptors.
The cleanup code fails to close the FD properly.
The process remains in an inconsistent state or leaks descriptors.
kept.impact: Resource exhaustion and possible denial of service.

kept.title: Race Condition in Path Reservations
kept.description: The `PathReservations` system relies on an asynchronous queue that could potentially be reordered or have items added while processing, causing overlaps.
steps_to_exploit: Submit highly concurrent requests for related paths.
The reservation queue logic has a race condition in the `#run` / `#clear` flow.
Two operations gain reservation for the same directory concurrently.
kept.impact: Filesystem race conditions, potentially allowing unauthorized file operations.

kept.title: Insecure Temporary File Deletion (Windows)
kept.description: The logic to handle non-atomic unlinks on Windows using renaming creates a predictable temporary filename structure (`.DELETE.<random_bytes>`).
steps_to_exploit: Predict or monitor the generation of `.DELETE` files on Windows.
Attempt to hijack the path during the rename/delete window.
This might allow a temporary file to be placed or accessed if the entropy of the random byte source is compromised.
kept.impact: Potential for local privilege escalation or temporary file hijacking.
